items.title: A tiny world model running games on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
items.reason: Runs two tiny int8 looped-transformer world models plus an MLP actor fully on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W (520KB SRAM, no_std Rust/embassy), generating and playing Breakout/Pong/Flappy Bird/Pac-Man-lite/Doom-lite on-device with on-device learning (Stream AC(lambda), no replay buffer); exact held-out frame accuracy 83.6-100% depending on game, firmware as small as 361KB flash. Real open-source repo (309 stars) with training code, Rust firmware, flashing script, and a WASM build — a concrete edge-inference-serving result.
key_facts: World model: looped transformer, 26k-131k params, int8 quantized; actor: float32 MLP, 9k-16k params
Runs on RP2350 (2 cores, FPU), 4MB flash, 520KB SRAM, no_std Rust on embassy
Exact held-out frame accuracy at 2 loops: Breakout 99.99%, Flappy Bird 100%, Pong 99.45%, Doom-lite 83.6%, Pac-Man 86.4%
Firmware footprint: 361KB flash/299KB RAM (Breakout) up to 600KB/460KB (Pac-Man)

key_facts: Affected versions 2.1.312/2.1.313 on macOS/Windows via Cursor Marketplace

Reverse SSH tunnel to 134.209.82.225 using -R *:0:localhost:22
Persistence via macOS LaunchAgent com.apple.sysmond.plist, Linux @reboot cron, Windows scheduled task
Beacon POSTs hostname/user/OS/public IP and names of KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|AWS|GCP env vars to :8099/beacon

items.title: Show HN: A working Nintendo in ~1GB of Qwen weights
items.reason: Compiles an NES 6502 CPU, 2KB RAM, and cartridge ROM into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B (using its Gated DeltaNet state as machine memory) so the model predicts the CPU's execution trace token-by-token; verified against nestest's golden log and runs real ROMs (Super Mario Bros and custom test games) at roughly 150-290x slower than a real NES. Builds on the earlier 'Qwenputer' (CHIP-8/RISC-V) project. Working CLI, test suite, demo GIFs.
key_facts: ~466.6M bf16 params but only 9.3M nonzero -> weights compress to 3.3MB
Speed: ~1,650 tok/s (numba), ~210 tok/s (numpy), ~10 tok/s (stock transformers); real NES needs ~700,000 tok/s
Verified exact match against nestest's golden CPU log for 3,348 instructions
Supports only NROM (mapper 0) cartridges, official opcodes only, no IRQs/sound
